messages.content: first satellite compared to the latest

message.content:
The **first artificial satellite** was **Sputnik 1**, launched by the Soviet Union on **October 4, 1957**.[1][2] It was very small by modern standards: about **58 cm** in diameter, weighed **83.6 kg**, and completed an orbit in about **98 minutes**.[1]

Compared with the **latest satellites**, Sputnik 1 was **tiny, simple, and short-lived**. Modern satellites are typically far larger and more capable, carrying advanced sensors, digital computers, high-throughput communications hardware, propulsion systems, and sometimes electric power generation far beyond what Sputnik had; Sputnik only transmitted radio beeps for a few weeks before its batteries ran out.[1][2]

If you mean a specific “latest satellite” — for example the newest Earth-observation, communications, or GPS satellite — I can compare Sputnik 1 against that exact satellite in a side-by-side table.
